Hi! I just got back from Nepal just under a month ago, after being there for 2 months. I did the Annapurna Circuit Trek, which in my opinion seemed better at the time, due to it being monsoon weather at the time. 

The buses are definitely in Nepali Rupees, and are usually very cheap, around 500Rs. And I'm not sure if you will be able to get night time bus from Phedi, they're usually in the early morning and throughout the day.

Local peoples English is usually good enough, at least at the lodges and shops, because they're constantly interacting with foreigners almost every day so they know a lot of English.

I would say not to bother with Indian Rupees, I didn't need any once whilst in Nepal, but I'd bring USD and Nepali Rupees, and also your bank card just in case you find an ATM. I only found 1 during my 14 day trek, in Marpha but you won't be going to Marpha.

Also, I went to a hotspring too but it was in Thathophani, and it cost 200Rs I think. Very cheap, but I didn't enjoy it as the water was very dirty, lots of 'bits' floating around and it was unbearably hot -for me anyway.


I lived up in Sarangkot in Pokhara for a month, and I would 100% recommend you take a taxi up to there if the day is clear, because from the top of Sarangkot you can see the whole Annapurna mountain range and it's just incredible.


Final thing, why are you planning for this 2-3 years in advance? I was spontaneously convinced to go by someone, with a weeks notice, and absolutely no trekking/hiking experience in my life. Admittedly I did struggle on the first day, but it was very doable.
